guide.summary: OpenProject documents OAuth applications with the api_v3 scope and an authorization code flow. Set up a developer-owned OAuth app on a test instance, then use the GET work packages list with offset and pageSize for pagination. Each customer instance needs its own registration, and the customer-side approval path is not fully documented. Keep the test read-only.

findings.title: Authorization code flow is documented
findings.detail: OpenProject documents an authorization code flow with an authorize URL, a token URL, and a Bearer token for API calls. Endpoints are relative to the customer's instance base URL.

evidence.quote: Enter the Name of your OAuth application.

https://example.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=<Client ID>&redirect_uri=<Redirect URI>&scope=<scope>&prompt=consent This requests redirects you to a URL that holds a code parameter which is the authentication code.
--header 'Authorization: Bearer <Token>' `

findings.title: Request the api_v3 scope for the standard API
findings.detail: api_v3 is the standard OpenProject API scope and is the default if no scope is checked. Work package visibility still depends on the connected user's permissions.

evidence.quote: Set the Scopes that the OAuth client application will be able to access. Multiple selection is possible. If no scope is checked, per default api_v3 is assumed. api_v3 is the
standard OpenProject API, while bcf_v2_1 is specific to the BIM edition of OpenProject.
